The search didn't turn up a documented way to manually restart Durable Objects. What it did cover is how gradual deployments affect the objects themselves.

- **Each object sticks to one version.** When you create a new gradual deployment, each Durable Object gets a Worker version based on your configured percentages, and that assignment holds until you create another deployment. Because only one version of each Durable Object can run at a time, the split works differently than it does for stateless Workers.
- **Objects reset when their version changes.** Cloudflare's docs say the Durable Object will only be reset when it is assigned a different version, so each Durable Object will only be reset once in this example. So the "restart" you're seeing is likely this reset, triggered by a version change rather than by a command you run.
- **Old and new code can briefly coexist.** Code changes for Workers and Durable Objects are released globally in an eventually consistent manner. A request on the newest Worker can reach an object still running older code for seconds to minutes. With gradual deployments, that window lasts as long as the live deployment keeps more than one version.
- **Worker and object code ship together.** A Worker bundle typically defines both the Durable Object class and the Worker that talks to it, so you cannot deploy changes to the Durable Object and its Worker independently. Cloudflare recommends that API changes between your Workers and Durable Objects be forward and backward compatible across code updates.
- **Rollback and limits.** Gradual deployments let you roll back to a previously stable version if you notice issues when deploying a new version. Also, you can only create a gradual deployment with the last 100 uploaded versions of your Worker.

If you need to force objects onto new code right away, the results don't show a supported method. The practical approach is to make your object-to-Worker APIs compatible across both versions, then let the gradual rollout move objects over as it progresses. I'd check the Durable Objects troubleshooting page linked in the docs for the reset behavior, since I didn't retrieve its contents.

content.text:
You can't delay the restart with a setting. A plain `wrangler deploy` moves every Durable Object to the new code, and each object is reset when its version changes. The closest option is **gradual deployments**: run `wrangler versions upload`, then `wrangler versions deploy` with a percentage split (for example, 90% old and 10% new). Cloudflare assigns each object to one version and keeps it there until your next deployment, so most objects keep running old code while you move the percentage up in steps. You can't pick which objects stay on the old version. Each object is still reset once when it moves to the new version, and requests from the new Worker code can reach objects still running old code. Make the API between your Worker and your Durable Objects work in both directions across versions.

Sources:
- [Gradual deployments with Durable Objects](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/versions-and-deployments/gradual-deployments/with-durable-objects/)
- [Gradual deployments](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/versions-and-deployments/gradual-deployments)
